items.title: Close the --seed non-finite determinism hole in pick()
items.acceptance: --seed Infinity and --seed -Infinity each return the identical aphorism on every run at exit 0, with the same filters applied
items.notes: CONDUCTOR-CONFIRMED defect (kickoff probe: 6 distinct aphorisms in 6 runs, exit 0). Resolution chosen: DETERMINISTIC PICK, not exit 2. Reasoning, judged against the SPEC's own rules: args.js already accepts Infinity as numeric (Number('Infinity') is not NaN) and the Domain rule promises determinism for --seed with no finiteness carve-out, so rejecting it would mean inventing a NEW undocumented validation rule rather than fixing the actual defect — which is that select.js gates its deterministic branch on Number.isFinite while toUint32Seed's IEEE-754 bit-fold already handles +/-Infinity deterministically. NaN stays exit 2 (parseSeedValue already rejects it) and that is correct and unchanged. Doc statement of this resolution belongs to I-3, which is why this item's files_hint is code+test only. NOT flagged route_class core despite playbook L-026: the allocator posture is trickle with allow_premium_pct 0 and opus at 96%, and gear 1's rule is S-effort sonnet builds — deliberately routing a 3-line fix to fable would spend premium the allocator has explicitly zeroed.

items.title: Mutation sweep of every documented behavior against the existing suite
items.acceptance: every documented flag and Domain-rule behavior has been mutated at least once against the current suite, and each surviving mutant is recorded with the exact mutation applied and the suite's response
items.notes: MEASUREMENT, not reading (playbook L-031). Behaviors to mutate: seed determinism, unseeded selection, --author case-insensitive matching, --tag membership matching, author+tag AND intersection, empty-set error contract, --list completeness and corpus order, --json single-line shape, the three exit codes, HELP content. Produces a survivor list ONLY. The HOLE-vs-BOUNDARY classification (L-033) is the CONDUCTOR's judgment and is deliberately withheld from this item: a survivor at a genuinely indiscriminable point (unseeded uniformity is the expected example) is the check being correct, and 'hardening' it produces a test that false-rejects honest output. Scratch copies for mutation must be whole-repo-minus-.git, never a hand-enumerated file subset (L-030).

items.title: Close HOLE survivors in the CLI-level suite
items.acceptance: each behavior the conductor classified HOLE is covered by a test that fails against its specific mutation, and whose removal lets that same mutation survive
items.notes: Admits tests ONLY for survivors the conductor classified HOLE — never for a surface that merely looks untested. Each test must be proven twice (L-029): failable against its mutation AND attributable, i.e. removing it lets the mutation survive. Planning-time hypotheses, to be settled by I-2a's actual measurement and not assumed: the current --list test asserts only a line-count floor and never order, and the current --json test uses JSON.parse after trim() so a pretty-printed multi-line mutant may still parse.

items.title: Close remaining HOLE survivors in the pure-module suite
items.acceptance: each remaining conductor-classified HOLE survivor in the parser or selection layer is covered by a test that fails against its specific mutation and whose removal lets that mutation survive
items.notes: Same twice-proven rule as I-2b. Scoped to test/args.test.js so it shares no file with I-2b (test/cli.test.js) or I-1 (test/select.test.js) — pairwise-disjoint even though this run's waves are size 1. If I-2a's survivors land entirely in one file, this item is closed as not-needed rather than padded with tests to justify its existence.

items.title: Settle the four doc/behaviour divergences identically in SPEC.md and README.md
items.acceptance: SPEC.md Domain rules and README.md state in matching wording: how --author matches, what --list does with --seed, what --list --json emits, and how a non-finite --seed behaves; and SPEC.md's OPEN AMBIGUITIES comment is gone rather than left open
items.notes: Four divergences, not three: the I-1 resolution is the fourth and is documented here rather than in I-1, keeping code and prose in separate file scopes. Documentation follows the SHIPPED behavior (--author is substring containment, case-insensitive) rather than changing behavior to match prose — changing the match semantics would be a user-visible behavior change, which the brief forbids. Depends on I-1 so the seed prose describes a resolution that has actually landed.

items.title: Corpus attribution triage — risk-ranked list for a human
items.acceptance: a written risk-ranked list names the corpus entries most likely to carry a wrong or unverifiable attribution with a stated reason each, and no file in the repo describes the corpus as audited, verified, or fact-checked
items.notes: TRIAGE, never an audit — nothing here can be confirmed without sources this run cannot reach, and the deliverable is explicitly a list for a human to settle (KI-2, T-006). Rank by internally-observable risk signals only: folklore maxims historically credited to several different people, wording that looks paraphrased or compressed rather than verbatim, entries already hedged as Anonymous (lowest risk, already honest), and entries traceable to a specific well-documented publication (lower risk). The stress-test's demo-embarrassment lens put this ABOVE the test items in value: a programming-aphorism CLI with misattributed quotes fails in exactly the way a green suite cannot see.

items.title: Repair or losslessly hand off the shared SWARM playbook file
items.acceptance: the shared playbook holds at most 20 lessons with no duplicate ids, following the file's own documented overflow rule, or is accompanied by a lossless archive of everything not carried forward plus a named reason for the handoff
items.notes: CONDUCTOR-EXECUTED, never dispatched: the file lives outside the target repo and hard rule 5 gives workflow agents target paths only. Current state: 31 lessons against a documented cap of 20, with L-023, L-025 and L-026 each naming two different lessons. Nothing is deleted without an archive first. Tracked as KI-5. The curation script bin/swarm-playbook.sh cannot be invoked from a headless session (allowlist gap), so any repair is a hand edit performed against the file's documented rules in playbook/README.md.

items.title: Refresh REPORT.md to the conductor-verified end-of-run state
items.acceptance: REPORT.md states the actual verified outcome of every I-item, and every item that was not conductor-verified is labeled unverified rather than claimed done
items.notes: Runs at WRAP_UP by design; depends on every other item because it reports their outcomes. Conductor-owned: reporting what was verified is the one thing that must not be delegated to an agent whose work is being reported on.
